newsitem.title: USA: USDA--CRP signup early 97, 24 Mln acres may shift.
newsitem.headline: USDA--CRP signup early 97, 24 Mln acres may shift.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department will hold a Conservation Reserve signup in early 1997 and up to 24 million acres, or two-thirds of total enrollment, could leave the reserve, officials said Wednesday.
The shift was possible because contracts expire on 24 million acres in fall 1997. Some of the land might be offered for re-enrollment.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said the goal was to see that productive farmland was in crop use and fragile land devoted to soil and water conservation and wildlife habitat.

During a news conference, Glickman and other USDA executives declined to estimate how much corn, wheat or soybean land would return to production under a set of proposed rules for operating the reserve through 2002.
They said they did not expect a dramatic shrinkage in Conservation Reserve enrollment nor much change in proportion of land in the reserve from various regions of the country.
In general, the new rules would bar land from the reserve unless it had an erodibility index of at least eight.
"Gone will be the days of retiring productive farmland," Glickman said, or using CRP to limit output of a crop.
